paraphrase: Allama questions Akka Mahādēvi: having renounced everything, why does she still cover her body with her hair? She answers that until the fruit ripens within, the rind does not fall, and that she covers the body's mark so as not to trouble others; the assembly acknowledges her attainment and she departs for Śrīśaila.

paraphrase: Every attainment tested in the book — devotion, work, knowledge, powers — is brought to the void (śūnya, bayalu), in which liṅga, aṅga and their union are no longer two; Allama is its embodiment.
